spans.text: LIGHTS GO LOW  ·  an original tone sketch, CC0
The hour between is not day and not night. It is
the light that has not noticed yet
that it is leaving. Nothing in it is quite finished, which is why
everything in it looks like a decision
Here are six small things that happen inside it. The grid below is one frame with
on: cards fill the row between a minimum and a maximum width, and the rows re-flow at every size.
They go first: a hundred black triangles agreeing on a horizon.
The water keeps the colour a minute longer than the sky does.
Every ridge draws a line, and the light stops to read it.
Somewhere a kitchen light comes on, and the evening becomes a place.
Sound travels better now. You can hear which village it is.
One by one, small decisions to stay awake.
Zoom in far enough and it is a room,
with a person in it, awake.
That was a spike: five scenes, one clip, two fonts and a handful of procedural images, all described as data and played by the runtime. If it felt like a page,
that is the thing to fix.
